root_cause: Two independent bugs prevent correct keyboard selection: (1) closeAllLists iterates forward over a live HTMLCollection while removing nodes, skipping every other list and leaving stale suggestion lists in the DOM; (2) navigationController.js adds the outer `navigate` function as the keydown listener instead of the inner `navigation` handler, causing event handling to break down and operate on stale lists.
repair_strategy: Fix closeAllLists to iterate backwards so all stale lists are removed. Fix navigationController to register the inner `navigation` function as the keydown listener, ensuring arrow-key and Enter handling uses the current suggestion list.
expected_accessibility_effect: Stale suggestion lists are fully removed, eliminating duplicate IDs. Keyboard navigation (ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Enter) now operates on the current list only, so the announced aria-selected item matches the committed form value. Screen readers will announce the correct selected option.
functional_risks: Backward iteration in closeAllLists is safe because removal order does not affect other logic.
Changing the listener from `navigate` to `navigation` aligns with the intended design; no other code depends on the old listener.
verification_requirements: After the sequence: focus #fruit, type 'b', ArrowDown ×2, type 'l', ArrowDown, Enter, the input value must be 'Blackberry'.
Confirm that no more than one element with ID 'autoComplete_list' exists in the DOM after each interaction.
Verify that ArrowDown and ArrowUp move aria-selected correctly through the filtered list.
Verify that Enter commits the currently highlighted suggestion.
